directAnswer: To reset a public IP address, you can either restart your modem or router, or request a new IP address from your Internet Service Provider (ISP).
summary: Resetting a public IP address can be done through hardware reset or ISP request, depending on your network configuration.

sections.heading: Resetting Your Modem or Router
sections.body: Restarting your modem or router can often result in a new public IP address, especially if your ISP uses dynamic IP addressing.

sections.heading: Requesting an IP Address Change from Your ISP
sections.body: If restarting your hardware does not yield a new IP address, you can contact your ISP and request a new public IP address.

steps.title: Restart Your Modem/Router
steps.detail: Unplug your modem or router from the power source, wait for about 5 minutes, then plug it back in and wait for it to fully restart.

steps.title: Contact Your ISP
steps.detail: Call or use the online support chat of your ISP to request a new public IP address. Be prepared to provide your account information.

faqs.question: Will resetting my public IP address affect my internet connection?
faqs.answer: Resetting your public IP address may temporarily disrupt your internet connection, but it should restore once the device reconnects.

faqs.question: How often can I reset my public IP address?
faqs.answer: You can reset your public IP address as often as needed, but the frequency may depend on your ISP's policies regarding IP allocation.

faqs.question: What if my ISP uses static IP addressing?
faqs.answer: If your ISP assigns a static IP address, you will need to contact them directly to change it, as it does not change on a reset.

caveats: Not all ISPs provide dynamic IP addresses; some may assign static IPs which do not change.
Restarting your modem/router may not guarantee a new IP address if your ISP has not released the old one.
